NFL DFS Week 2 Picks: Top DraftKings Projections, Values and Sim Plays

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, September 20 · 13 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of September 19, 9:25 PM ET

Bijan Robinson carries the highest SPAGS model projection on the Week 2 DraftKings main slate: 25.1 DraftKings points at $8,200. He also holds 37% of the simulated winning-lineup credit across 10,000 simulations, more than any other player on the slate, with Derrick Henry second at 26% for $7,200.

Behind Robinson, the model's next four projections are Christian McCaffrey (22.3, $8,000), Derrick Henry (21.8, $7,200), De'Von Achane (20.8, $6,700) and Jaxon Smith-Njigba (19.4, $8,100). De'Von Achane returns the most per dollar of that group at 3.10 projected points per $1,000. Jaxon Smith-Njigba leads the wide receivers at 19.4 for $8,100, Brock Purdy leads the quarterbacks at 18.8 for $6,200, and Trey McBride leads the tight ends at 16.1 for $6,900.

The 13-game slate runs from a 50.5-point total in WAS at DAL down to 39.5 in PHI at TEN. Every projection below is a SPAGS model estimate from the September 19, 9:25 PM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. Winning-lineup credit comes from 10,000 simulations of the contest, and tied winning entries share credit. A player's simulated floor is his 10th-percentile score and his ceiling is his 95th.

Quarterbacks: Week 2 DraftKings projections

Brock Purdy, SF vs MIA ($6,200)

Brock Purdy carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 18.8 DraftKings points at $6,200. That is 0.1 points clear of Drake Maye. The model includes 3.5 rushing attempts. The salary works out to 3.02 projected points per $1,000, 9th of 20 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Purdy averaged 18.7 points with a simulated floor of 7.5 and a ceiling of 34.2, and he holds 8% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. San Francisco is a 13.5-point favorite at home against Miami, with an implied team total of 29 in a game totaled at 44.5.

Drake Maye, NE vs PIT ($6,100)

Drake Maye projects 2nd at the position with 18.7 DraftKings points at $6,100. The model includes 5.0 rushing attempts. The salary works out to 3.06 projected points per $1,000, 8th of 20 at the position. Across 10,000 simulations Maye averaged 18.8 points with a simulated floor of 7.4 and a ceiling of 34.5, and he holds 8% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. New England is a 5.5-point favorite at home against Pittsburgh, with an implied team total of 23.5 in a game totaled at 41.5.

Value: Carson Wentz, MIN at CHI ($4,600)

Carson Wentz projects for 15.8 DraftKings points at $4,600, which works out to 3.44 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 20 quarterbacks the model projects for 15 or more points. Across 10,000 simulations Wentz averaged 15.9 points with a simulated floor of 6.2 and a ceiling of 28.6, and he holds 4% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Minnesota is a 4.5-point underdog on the road against Chicago, with an implied team total of 21.5 in a game totaled at 47.5.
